Docs / Getting started

A guide to Capital.

Company research, treasury records, and your portfolio. All in one place.

Capital helps you explore businesses and understand how investment records, holder allocations, and distributions fit together.

01

Explore a business

Browse by sector or investment type. Each profile includes the business, its offering structure, and links to the original provider. Use those sources to check current terms and availability.

02

Follow the treasury

View recorded purchase costs, cash, reserves, and payment activity. The business directory is a research list; a treasury position requires its own purchase record.

03

Read your portfolio

Connect a wallet to read its test balances and claim records, or choose Preview a holder to explore an interactive example.

A few useful distinctions

Research
A company profile or watchlist entry.
Investment record
A purchase reference, its cost, and supporting evidence.
Holder allocation
The portion attributed to a holder under the applicable rules.
Distribution
A funded payment or a separately documented equity transfer.

Docs / Ownership

Understand what you hold.

The investment documents define the rights. Onchain records make the allocation easier to follow.

Investment types

TypeWhat the record represents
Company sharesOwnership in the issuer, with rights set by the share class and agreements.
Beneficial interestAn interest in an underlying investment held through a custody or other legal arrangement.
Vehicle or SPV interestAn interest in an entity that holds the investment. Your rights follow the vehicle’s documents.
SAFEAn agreement that may convert into equity if its specified conditions occur.
Loan or noteContractual payment rights under the debt terms.

Further reading: Wefunder’s guide to investment structures ↗.

What makes an equity holding verifiable?

  • An identified issuer, security type, and quantity.
  • Accepted purchase documents and recognized ownership records.
  • A documented allocation to the holder, including applicable eligibility and transfer restrictions.
  • A clear link between the holder’s identity, wallet, and records.

A wallet balance alone does not establish ownership of a business. A document hash identifies a file’s bytes; it does not verify the document’s authenticity or legal effect.

Provider example

Animoca Brands on Republic

Republic describes its Animoca product as a 1:1 beneficial ownership interest in custodied ordinary shares. That describes the provider’s product; appearing in Capital’s directory is a research reference.

Read the original offering ↗

Capital participation units

The wallet treasury uses nontransferable test units to calculate allocations. These units are separate from company shares and from a Pons launch token. The portfolio labels example allocations and equity records separately.

Docs / Treasury & fees

Follow the flow of funds.

Capital’s investment funding comes from Pons creator fees.

The plan uses creator fees allocated to Capital, without collecting investment deposits from holders. Record the funding source separately from the legal owner of each investment.

From creator fees to business holdings

  1. Record the fee withdrawal. Identify the launch, network, fee asset, amount, transaction and receiving wallet. Pending or claimable fees are not treasury receipts.
  2. Reconcile funds available to invest. Match the treasury receipt and record any conversion, transfer costs and reserves. Use the payment asset and network accepted by the selected offering.
  3. Complete the provider purchase. The authorized account owner completes payment and signs the provider’s documents. Keep the order reference, payment confirmation and final holding statement together.
  4. Record the actual holding. Record the legal buyer, issuer, security type, quantity and cost after the provider confirms the purchase. A winning community vote does not create a holding.

Read the treasury

Creator fees received
Verified payouts from Capital’s launch received by its designated wallet. Pending fees and protocol-wide totals are separate.
Available funds
Reconciled funds available after purchase commitments, costs, and reserves. An unconnected balance is shown as unavailable.
Invested at cost
Documented company purchase cost. This is not a current market valuation.
Company investments
The issuer, legal owner, exact security, shares or units, purchase cost, provider, and ownership evidence. A SAFE or note is recorded as that instrument, rather than as issued shares.
Creator-fee receipts
The receipt date, asset, amount, receiving wallet, and supporting transaction.

Creator fees and holder distributions

Funding an investment with creator fees does not automatically give token holders company shares or a right to its income. Holder allocations and distributions follow the separately documented ownership and eligibility rules.

Fees and investment proceeds

A creator-fee receipt, a purchase, a principal repayment, and investment income are different events. Record them separately so the ledger shows where funds came from and how they were used.

In the test treasury, principal repayments reduce investment cost. Recorded income can fund a distribution; purchase reservations and reserves are accounted for separately.

Pons

Launchpad fees and treasury income

Pons V2 pays creator fees in the launch’s pairing asset; fees are not necessarily USDC. The fee asset, recipient and terms must be checked for Capital’s actual launch. Creator trading fees are separate from a portfolio company’s dividends or sale proceeds.

Reconcile a provider withdrawal with the receiving wallet and the treasury deposit record. A token launch by itself does not create an investment record or a holder’s equity rights.

Read Pons fee documentation ↗

Keep the evidence with the plan

In Launch setup, record creator-fee receipt references and the settlement route. The review packet can include fingerprints for a creator-fee withdrawal, settlement confirmation, treasury receipt and final holding statement. These are local document references, not uploaded or independently verified records.

Open the purchase worksheet ↗

Use the treasury tools

Expand Test treasury tools at the bottom of Treasury to access the separate rehearsal. Its controls let you select a test network, refresh test balances, copy a test treasury link, or manage test deposits and records. View ledger shows the transaction history.

About mUSD The treasury’s test-dollar token has no cash value or redemption promise. It is used to exercise deposits, records, allocations, and claims.

Docs / Holdings & distributions

Know your allocation.

Your portfolio separates investment records, available claims, and completed distributions.

Read a business holding

Each row identifies the company and investment type. Attributed cost shows the portion assigned to the holder using the applicable participation units. Cost is not a quoted market price, a withdrawal balance, or a count of company shares.

Equity quantities belong in a separate record supported by a verified purchase and a documented allocation to the holder.

How cash claims work

  1. Fund the distribution. The administrator commits the total amount to the contract.
  2. Fix each wallet’s allocation. The contract records the eligible wallets and their payout amounts. Later participation changes do not rewrite that distribution.
  3. Claim from the eligible wallet. The wallet signs its claim, and a successful transaction creates a receipt. The same allocation cannot be claimed twice.
Worked example · mUSD

A 1,000 mUSD distribution

Holder A · 60 of 100 units600 mUSD
Holder B · 40 of 100 units400 mUSD

The interactive holder preview uses this example. Its claim button simulates a payment within the page; connected-wallet claims use the selected testnet contract.

Cash and equity distributions

A cash claim transfers the funded payment asset. An equity distribution requires its own security type, quantity, allocation date, and supporting ownership records. Receiving a cash payment does not itself transfer company shares.

Download your records

Use Download holder statement in the connected portfolio to export its loaded investment references and claim receipts. For a particular transaction, keep the network, contract, transaction hash, and supporting documents together.

Open My portfolio ↗

Docs / Wallet setup

Connect your wallet.

Your wallet identifies your account and signs the transactions you approve.

  1. Choose Connect wallet. Select an installed MetaMask wallet, or use the QR option with MetaMask mobile.
  2. Review the connection. Check the account and permissions in MetaMask. Connecting is separate from signing a treasury transaction.
  3. Choose your treasury. Open an existing treasury by address or deploy a test treasury using the page’s setup controls.
  4. Review each transaction. Check the network, contract, asset, and amount before signing. Confirmed records appear after the transaction is included.

Docs / FAQs & sources

A few clear answers.

The details behind the company directory, portfolio, and treasury.

Does a listed company mean Capital owns it?

No. The directory contains research candidates. Verified ownership requires a purchase and supporting ownership records for the holder’s allocation.

Does holding a token give me shares in every business?

Rights depend on the specific security and legal agreements. A launch token or test participation unit does not automatically grant shares in the companies shown in the directory.

Are distributions guaranteed?

No. A claim requires a funded allocation. Real investments may produce no regular income and can lose value.

Why do my current units differ from a past payment?

Each distribution keeps the wallet allocations fixed when it was funded. Current participation units can change without changing a past distribution.

How do I talk to the community?

Open Community, then Forum. Sign in to post a message or reply. Messages are shared with people who have access to Capital and refresh every 10 seconds while you read the latest page. You can remove and restore your own posts; an administrator can moderate messages. Posting does not submit a vote. Open the forum ↗

What does Community voting do?

An administrator publishes a reviewed shortlist with a token, voting rule, and voting window. Eligible holders sign a ballot with MetaMask. Capital verifies the signature and the token balance at the fixed opening snapshot before recording a shared receipt. One current ballot per wallet counts; a new accepted ballot replaces the previous choice before closing. Open Community voting ↗

Can I invest directly through a provider?

A company profile links to its original offering. The provider determines availability, eligibility, account requirements, and terms. Capital does not submit orders through your Republic or Wefunder account.

What are Capital investment rounds?

Capital rounds organize investment decisions separately from a company fundraising round. Drafts live in shared storage and only the administrator can edit or publish them. Published terms are fixed. Material changes pause voting and require a new revision with fresh reviews and fresh ballots. A result does not purchase a business or create portfolio holdings. Open investment rounds ↗

How are voting results kept accurate?

The server counts the latest accepted ballot for each wallet using integer token amounts. Eligibility is read from the last finalized block at or before opening, after a later timestamp has finalized. If historical data cannot be verified, voting waits. The page refreshes shared data every 30 seconds while visible; closed results are locked with a digest and signed receipts. Administrator review dates identify when offering documents were checked; they are not a live provider feed.

Which wallets and voting rules are supported?

MetaMask and standard EVM account signatures are supported. Smart-contract wallet signatures are not enabled. Each round chooses token-weighted voting or one vote per eligible wallet, with a minimum balance at the opening snapshot. One wallet does not prove one person, and the voting token does not by itself represent company equity. The network must provide historical ERC-20 reads and finalized block data.

    OWNERSHIP, EXPLAINED

    How onchain equity works.

    A token can represent real ownership when legal rights and recognized ownership records connect it to an investment.

    U.S. research overview · reviewed September 13, 2026 · Capital’s jurisdiction and investor eligibility are undecided.

    01Legal ownership

    An entity buys a permitted investment.

    02Documented rights

    Agreements define what holders own.

    03Onchain record

    Verified wallets track permitted interests.

    04Distributions

    Actual proceeds follow the agreed terms.

    Three ways a token can connect to equity

    COMPANY SHARES

    Issuer-sponsored shares

    The company or its agent links token transfers to its official shareholder records. Rights follow the share class.

    SHARES HELD IN CUSTODY

    Beneficial ownership

    A custody arrangement can give token holders an indirect interest in shares. The ownership relationship must be legally established.

    INTEREST IN A VEHICLE

    A Capital company or fund

    The entity would own the investments. Eligible holders would own documented interests in Capital, with distributions governed by its agreements.

    The SEC staff’s tokenization statement distinguishes ownership-backed arrangements from synthetic price exposure. Tokenization does not remove securities-law requirements.

    THE ROUTE TO INVESTIGATE FOR CAPITAL

    Own an interest in the investment vehicle.

    A vehicle that holds approved Republic or Wefunder investments could define holder participation and distributions. It must first qualify under the applicable offering, fund and adviser rules. This is a proposed direction for review, not an approved structure.

    Republic Note is a useful example: it represents Class B LLC membership interests with specified economic rights. It does not give holders direct shares in every portfolio company, and its regulatory treatment cannot simply be copied.

    Investor access changes the route

    Private / accredited investors

    A private fund may combine an Investment Company Act exclusion with an offering exemption. These are separate requirements. Adviser obligations also need review. One possible fundraising route is Rule 506(c), which requires verified accredited purchasers.

    SEC: private funds ↗Rule 506(c) requirements ↗

    Retail investors

    Reg CF’s crowdfunding-vehicle exception is a conduit for a single class of securities from one issuer. It does not cover a treasury picking many businesses. Broad retail access for an investment pool requires a separate structure and regulatory analysis.

    Crowdfunding vehicle rule ↗

    What needs to happen before a real allocation?

    • Accepted purchase: the provider permits the entity, investment and intended use. The holding might be stock, a SAFE, or an SPV interest.
    • Holder agreement: defines ownership, allocations, costs, voting and any distribution rights.
    • Recognized records: quantity, acquisition evidence, custodian or issuer confirmation, and wallet-to-holder reconciliation.
    • Permitted transfers: investor eligibility and transfer restrictions are enforced. Moving a token alone cannot override them.
    • Actual distributable proceeds: payments use received funds and the agreed allocation. Equity may produce no regular income.

    See Wefunder’s ownership structures and transfer process.

    Does fee funding create a loophole?

    Using creator fees to buy investments does not, by itself, settle the vehicle’s legal status or create holder ownership. A business primarily investing in securities may be an investment company. A DAO label or a different blockchain does not establish an exemption.

    SEC: investment-company status ↗

    Pons can be part of a proposed token and fee flow. No Capital token with documented equity rights has been launched. A security token would need compatible ownership and transfer controls; support on Pons and Robinhood Chain has not been established.

    What Capital supports today

    Real-company research, a local voting preview, and testnet treasury records. No real investments, equity issuance or cash payouts are active. Securities counsel and the funding provider must establish the live structure before these can be enabled.

    TEST PARTICIPATION

    Units for testing payouts.

    The treasury administrator assigns nontransferable test units to up to 100 wallets. They are used only to calculate a test distribution.

    1. Current units show current participation

      Attributed test cost uses your units divided by the total assigned units. It is not a withdrawable treasury balance.

    2. Each distribution freezes an allocation

      The contract funds the total and records each wallet’s payout at the transaction’s block. Later unit changes do not change existing allocations.

    3. Claims pay the eligible wallet once

      Only the allocated wallet can claim its mUSD. Test dollars have no cash value and cannot buy real company shares.

    These units are not the Pons launch token or an equity-backed token. Actual holder rights, eligibility, and a production token-to-interest formula have not been established.
